source.orientation_reason: Source long axis is Y; the broad bottom disc is at source Y minimum, so +90 degrees about X maps the tower top toward +Z.

orientation.visual_basis: The unicorn relief and projecting catch tray face -Y after the +90 degree X rotation.

spiral.description: Faceted helical slide descending around the elliptical core axis; tread facets are rounded slab segments fused to the shell with radial overlap. The top surface is continuous (no vertical risers), so the turn-to-turn pitch is the governing dice clearance.
spiral.entry_note: Blade start sits 6 mm below the inlet opening floor (Z=118), so every die dropped into the back inlet lands on the spiral.
spiral.exit_note: The blade ends at azimuth -45 degrees (front-right of the ellipse) with motion direction about 30 degrees left of straight-forward, aiming toward the outlet; the die then drops about 2 mm onto the closed base floor and rolls out through the outlet onto the tray.
spiral.post: No central post. A 22 mm cube cannot both roll around a central column and fit the 24.5 mm minor core radius; the inner void is 32 x 10 mm, smaller than a 22 mm die, so dice bridge it and cannot fall through.

die_path.proxy: axis-aligned 22 mm bounding cube; on the spiral it rides as a sliding block parallel to the local slope, analytically lifted about 1.2 mm above the surface. Geometric clearance proof, not a contact simulation.
die_path.pose_note: Each spiral waypoint carries [tangent_azimuth, tilt] so the 22 mm verification cube sits as a sliding block parallel to the local slope; entry/floor waypoints are upright.

manufacturing.fit_intent: Free-fall spiral descent for common polyhedral dice; no mating fit.
manufacturing.load_direction: Gravity along -Z; spiral facets carry intermittent die impacts into the side shell.
manufacturing.support_assumption: The spiral pitch of about 36.4 mm over roughly 130 mm of arc gives a gentle slope (~15.5 degrees) that is close to self-supporting. Opening crowns may still bridge or need localized tree support.

assumptions: The normalized source has no reliable embedded units, so 100 mm/source-unit gives an approximately 199 mm tall tower.
The flattened artistic body requires an elliptical rather than circular core; 22 mm is the validated design proxy, while 24 mm dice are not claimed.

Discrete riser-based stairs with 6-8 full steps cannot carry a 22 mm die in the 94 mm usable span (each true riser needs about 27 mm). The validated alternative is this faceted helical slide with 20 tread facets over 2.4 turns.
Automated path clearance does not prove real-world tumbling; a physical 22 mm die test is required.
